es: Escribir un relato breve con narrador en primera persona, tiempos narrativos variados (pasado simple, continuo y perfecto), un símil y una oración enfática.

teaching.en: The narrator tells the story and describes the scene.
teaching.es: El narrador cuenta la historia y describe la escena.
teaching.explanationEs: El narrador suele usar el pasado; eligiendo bien el tiempo se ve qué es escenario y qué es acción.
teaching.audioText: The narrator tells the story and describes the scene.

teaching.en: It was raining when I reached the station.
teaching.es: Llovía cuando llegué a la estación.
teaching.explanationEs: Past continuous (was raining) para el escenario; past simple (reached) para la acción puntual.
teaching.audioText: It was raining when I reached the station.

teaching.en: When I arrived, the last train had already left.
teaching.es: Cuando llegué, el último tren ya había salido.
teaching.explanationEs: Past perfect (had left): algo que pasó antes de otro momento del pasado.
teaching.audioText: When I arrived, the last train had already left.

teaching.en: The silence between us was like a wall.
teaching.es: El silencio entre nosotros era como un muro.
teaching.explanationEs: Un símil con like da una imagen: el silencio se compara con un muro.
teaching.audioText: The silence between us was like a wall.

teaching.en: What I remember most is the smell of rain.
teaching.es: Lo que más recuerdo es el olor de la lluvia.
teaching.explanationEs: What + oración + is: énfasis en lo que quieres destacar.
teaching.audioText: What I remember most is the smell of rain.

teaching.en: It was the old key that opened the door.
teaching.es: Fue la vieja llave la que abrió la puerta.
teaching.explanationEs: It was + cosa + that/who: énfasis en quién o qué hizo la acción.
teaching.audioText: It was the old key that opened the door.

feedback.es: El escenario del pasado usa was/were + -ing: It was raining.

hint.es: El escenario del pasado usa was/were + -ing.

origin.text: It ___ raining when I left home.

prompt.es: Elige la frase correcta sobre algo que ocurrió antes.

choices.text: When Mia arrived, the film already began.
When Mia arrived, the film had already begun.
When Mia arrived, the film was already beginning.

feedback.es: Had + participio (had already begun) marca que la película empezó antes de la llegada de Mia.

hint.es: Lo anterior a otro momento del pasado usa had + participio.

origin.text: Mia arrived at eight. The film began at seven.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La casa olía como un viejo libro.»

answer.text: The house smelled like an old book

feedback.es: Smelled like + nombre forma un símil olfativo: la casa se compara con un libro viejo.

hint.es: Usa like para comparar la casa con un libro.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del relato con su función.

pairs: Her smile was like a bright light.

feedback.es: Was getting dark pinta el escenario, opened es la acción, had lost es lo anterior y like a bright light es un símil.

pairs: Her smile was like a bright light.

prompt.es: Escucha el principio de un relato y elige qué ocurrió antes.

choices.text: They arrived before the film began.
They waited outside before buying tickets.
The film started before they arrived.

feedback.es: Had already started indica que la película empezó antes de que llegaran.

origin.audio: When we got to the cinema, the film had already started, so we bought some snacks and waited.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que enfatiza lo que más recuerda el narrador.

choices.text: What I remember most is the smell of the bakery.
I remember most what is the smell of the bakery.
It is the smell of the bakery what I remember.

feedback.es: What I remember most is… es la estructura enfática; «it is the smell what I remember» es un calco del español.

origin.text: The narrator wants to stress the smell of the bakery.

prompt.es: Elige el tiempo adecuado para describir el escenario de la escena.

choices.text: It is getting dark when we left the café.
It was getting dark when we left the café.
It has got dark when we left the café.

feedback.es: Was getting dark (continuo) describe el escenario mientras ocurre la acción de salir del café.

origin.text: Describe the background of the scene: it was evening, and the light was changing slowly.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué ocurrió primero.

choices.text: He made tea before his sister went to bed.
He sat in the kitchen before he reached the house.
His sister went to bed before he arrived.

feedback.es: Had already gone to bed indica que la hermana se acostó antes de que Leo llegara.

origin.audio: When Leo reached the house, his sister had already gone to bed, so he made some tea and sat in the kitchen.

prompt.es: Completa: «Fue mi abuela quien encontró la llave.»

feedback.es: It was + persona + who destaca quién encontró la llave.

origin.text: It was my grandmother ___ found the key.

prompt.es: Escribe el relato: dos tiempos narrativos, un símil y una oración enfática.

answer.text: It was raining when I reached the station, and my bag was heavy. I had promised Sara that I would be there at eight, but the last train had already left. The station was almost empty. A man was sleeping on a bench, and there was a small clock above the ticket office. I felt cold and afraid. What I remember most is the silence, which was like a wall between me and the rest of the city. I took out my phone, but my phone had no power. Then I heard a voice behind me. It was my old teacher who was standing there with an umbrella! She had seen me from the bus and had followed me inside. She laughed, gave me her phone and said, “Call Sara. She has probably been waiting for you.” I called, and Sara answered at once. She was not angry. In fact, she had missed the train too, and she was waiting at the next station. My teacher bought us all a hot drink while we waited for the next train. We talked about the long day, about our families and about the rain. We met Sara an hour later, and we laughed about the whole night. I will never forget how kind both of them were.
accepted: It was raining when I reached the station, and my bag was heavy. I had promised Sara that I would be there at eight, but the last train had already left. The station was almost empty. A man was sleeping on a bench, and there was a small clock above the ticket office. I felt cold and afraid. What I remember most is the silence, which was like a wall between me and the rest of the city. I took out my phone, but my phone had no power. Then I heard a voice behind me. It was my old teacher who was standing there with an umbrella! She had seen me from the bus and had followed me inside. She laughed, gave me her phone and said, “Call Sara. She has probably been waiting for you.” I called, and Sara answered at once. She was not angry. In fact, she had missed the train too, and she was waiting at the next station. My teacher bought us all a hot drink while we waited for the next train. We talked about the long day, about our families and about the rain. We met Sara an hour later, and we laughed about the whole night. I will never forget how kind both of them were.

It was getting dark when I arrived at the cinema, and a long line was waiting outside. I had bought the tickets two days before, but when I looked in my bag, I understood that I had left them at home. My heart was beating like a drum. What I felt most was shame, because Leo had already told everyone that the film was his idea. I walked to the desk and explained the problem. The woman smiled and said, “Do not worry. Show me the message on your phone.” I looked for it, but my hands were shaking. Finally I found it. It was a small miracle that the message was still there! She checked the name, printed two new tickets and wished us a good film. When I found Leo, the film had already started, so we sat in the dark and whispered like children. Afterwards we walked home and he laughed at me all the way. I remember that night as the day I learned to check my bag twice, and I also remember the woman at the desk, who was kinder than I deserved.

feedback.es: Un buen relato usa el continuo para el escenario, el pasado simple para la acción, el perfecto para lo anterior, un símil con like o as y una oración enfática.

origin.text: Escribe un relato en primera persona de 200 a 250 palabras sobre una noche en que llegaste tarde a un lugar importante (una estación, un cine, una fiesta). Usa al menos dos tiempos narrativos (por ejemplo, past continuous para el escenario y past perfect para lo anterior), un símil con like o as y una oración enfática (What… is… o It was… who/that…).

prompt.es: Elige la frase que contiene un símil.

choices.text: The room was as quiet as a library.
The room was a quiet library.
The quiet room whispered a secret.

feedback.es: As quiet as a library compara con as…as: es un símil; las otras opciones son metáfora y personificación.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué recuerda más la hablante.

choices.text: The crowd, more than the sea.
The sea, more than the crowd.
The weather, more than the sea.

feedback.es: What I remember most is… destaca el sonido del mar frente a la multitud.

origin.audio: What I remember most is the sound of the sea, not the crowd.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Cuando ella llamó, yo ya había salido de casa.»

answer.text: When she called I had already left home

feedback.es: Had already left marca que salir ocurrió antes de la llamada.
